title: Find the card numbers customers type into support tickets

blocks.text: Every night support exports its tickets to an analytics vendor. Before the vendor is allowed to receive them, the compliance team wants a report of the tickets that hold card numbers, so that those can be cleaned first and the vendor can stay out of scope.

Customers type card numbers the way they read them off the card, in groups, with spaces or dashes or neither. Support staff paste lines from terminal logs. Tickets also hold dates, phone numbers, order numbers and case references.
`CardNumberFinder.find` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/CardNumberFinder.java` already walks the ticket and builds the report. Finish the three methods marked `TODO`:

items: `candidates()`: what in a ticket might be a card number;
`shown(...)`: how a card number appears in the report.

blocks.text: When you're done, the report lists every card number in a ticket, where it starts, and in a form that is safe to hand around, and nothing else. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: card numbers typed in groups with spaces or dashes are found where they start, and the report says which card each was
a ticket with dates, phone numbers and order numbers but no card number has no findings
a number of card length whose last digit is not its check digit is not reported
a 15-digit card typed in groups of four, six and five is found, not only groups of four
a card number with a letter right before it, as in a pasted track 1, is found
card-length digits that are part of a longer run of digits are not reported
the report shows each card number masked, never in clear

origin.section: 13.2. A Card Number Is Recognised by Its Length and Its Check Digit

concepts: A card number is 13 to 19 digits that are not part of a longer run and end in a valid Luhn check digit; a scan's hits are places to look at, and its report is masked.
